translations.answer: The original thread does not support treating it as a general solution. Early users reported that the workaround appears usable, but additional mounting body masses can cause measurement bias. Later users reported that soft weld constraints cause the tendon to stretch while passing through the mounting body, and the solref="0.0002 1" can only partially improve the situation. Since no maintainer has validated or established a unified error bound, the thread must be compared against known tendon force in the target model.
translations.applicability: This is experimental within MuJoCo models; validation of mounting body mass, weld solref, elongation, and phase error is required.
translations.credibility.rationale: The solution has not closed or there are unresolved conflicts in the sources.
translations.details.attempts.0: Use a free mounting body as the tendon attachment point, weld it to the target body, and measure the weld force.
translations.details.attempts.1: A user adjusted the weld solref to 0.0002 1 and reported that elongation is only partially improved.
translations.details.attempts.2: Calculate passive force and read tendonlimitfrc separately according to the maintainer's final suggestion.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between passive spring/damper force and tendon limit constraint force, do not sum a zero-value site sensor as both.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Compare the tendon spring/damper calculation in engine_passive.c with the constraint force definition in the XML reference.
translations.details.diagnostics.2: If using a welded mounting body, check the mass, weld softness, and tendon elongation.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: For passive force, calculate according to the official engine source code's tendon spring/damper definition; for constraint force, use sensor/tendonlimitfrc; sum the two when total force is required.
translations.details.environments.0: MuJoCo public Issue #832, 2023–2025 replies; passive tendon, tendon limit constraint, and site/weld force sensor.
translations.details.environments.1: Official source code locates the issue in engine_passive.c, lines 377–415, commit 100b1a06fd8f6a184a3e495adff3ff044b1ff4f2.
translations.details.limits.0: The frc_spring in the engine source is a local calculation variable and should not be rewritten as a stable, public API name.
translations.details.limits.1: tendonlimitfrc only represents the tendon limit constraint force and does not automatically include passive spring and damper forces.
translations.details.limits.2: The welded mounting body workaround has not been validated by the maintainer and is associated with known softness and mass errors.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Original thread user confirms that the passive spring force calculation is effective for their model.
translations.details.outcomes.1: The site sensor directly misses the tendon force, and this issue has not been marked as fixed in this Issue.
translations.details.outcomes.2: The welded mounting body workaround results in conflicting outcomes across different models.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Why does the force sensor at the tendon attachment point not return the tendon force?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: How can one separately obtain the passive tendon force, the tendon limit constraint force, and the total force?
translations.details.problem_statements.2: Is the measurement of tendon force via welded mounting body reliable?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Before using simulation tendon force for real machine limit force or protection, apply known load calibration to the passive force, constraint force, and sensor sign.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: The project collaborator confirmed that the site force sensor missed the tendon force at the time.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The error in the weld workaround is related to extra mounting body mass and weld softness, but the original thread lacks a general error model.
translations.details.symptoms.0: When there is force on the tendon, the force sensor at the attachment point still reads zero.
translations.details.symptoms.1: The welded mounting body workaround causes elongation and force deviation in some models.
translations.source.locator: Issue #832, workaround issuecomment-1816986241; elongation counterexample issuecomment-2500739225; solref partial improvement issuecomment-2500866159
translations.source.title: Gap in Site Force Sensor, Force Decomposition, and Welded Mounting Body Scheme for MuJoCo Tendon Force Measurement
translations.title: Can one attach the tendon to a free mounting body, weld it to the target body, and read the weld force as a general tendon force sensor?
